title: Button Bounce Oscilloscope
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Clocks and Watches with AI
description: A single-shot oscilloscope captures contact bounce on every press; adjust the debounce window and a 0.1 uF hardware filter until one press counts once.

learningObjectives: Analyze how contact bounce turns one press into several falling edges
Evaluate how long a software debounce window must be to count each press once
Compare software debouncing with a hardware RC filter
prerequisites: Pull-up resistors and active-low buttons from Chapter 5

accessibility.notes: Controls are standard HTML form elements; the canvas has a describe() text for screen readers

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Measure-and-tune investigation (single-shot capture instead of a continuously scrolling trace)
keyQuestions: Why does one press produce several falling edges?
What window length is long enough, and what is too long?
How does the capacitor stop the extra edges?
commonMisconceptions: A counter that jumps by 3 means the wiring is wrong
A longer debounce window is always better
assessmentOpportunities: Students choose a window longer than the longest bounce and justify it with data from the scope.
Students explain why the hardware filter produces one falling edge.
Students relate the slider to `DEBOUNCE_MS` in the chapter's code.

controls.label: Press button
controls.description: Captures a new random bounce burst

controls.label: Span
controls.description: Sets the scope time span to 20, 50 or 150 ms

controls.label: Hardware filter (0.1 uF capacitor)
controls.description: Smooths the trace with an RC filter

controls.label: Debounce window
controls.description: Software debounce window from 0 to 100 ms
